questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If doctors had detected the illness earlier, the patient wouldn't be suffering now.
If doctors detected the illness earlier, the patient wouldn't be suffering now.
If doctors had detected the illness earlier, the patient wouldn't have suffered now.
If doctors had detected the illness earlier, the patient won't suffer now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If doctors had detected..., the patient wouldn't be suffering now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The disease will keep spreading unless people won't get vaccinated.
The disease will keep spreading unless people get vaccinated.
The disease will keep spreading unless that people get vaccinated.
The disease will keep spreading without people get vaccinated.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless people get vaccinated.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new treatments has been approved this year.
Several new treatments have approved this year.
Several new treatments have been approved this year.
Several new treatments have being approved this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been approved this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This shortage of medicine should addressed immediately.
This shortage of medicine should being addressed immediately.
This shortage of medicine should be address immediately.
This shortage of medicine should be addressed immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be addressed immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please take this medicine twice a day.")
options: The doctor told me to take the medicine twice a day.
The doctor told me take the medicine twice a day.
The doctor said me to take the medicine twice a day.
The doctor told me that take the medicine twice a day.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told me to take the medicine twice a day.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should exercise more regularly.")
options: She suggested to exercise more regularly.
She suggested exercising more regularly.
She suggested me exercising more regularly.
She suggested that I exercising more regularly.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested exercising more regularly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The clinic which she works for it treats low-income patients.
The clinic for that she works treats low-income patients.
The clinic for which she works treats low-income patients.
The clinic she works for which treats low-income patients.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the clinic for which she works.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The study publishing last week revealed a rise in heart disease.
The study published last week reveal a rise in heart disease.
The study which published last week revealed a rise in heart disease.
The study published last week revealed a rise in heart disease.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The study published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The patient must have skipped several doses of the medication.
The patient must skipped several doses of the medication.
The patient must have skip several doses of the medication.
The patient must has skipped several doses of the medication.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have skipped several doses.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The hospital should acted sooner to isolate the patient.
The hospital should have acted sooner to isolate the patient.
The hospital should have act sooner to isolate the patient.
The hospital should has acted sooner to isolate the patient.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Life expectancy rose significantly over the past century.
Life expectancy has risen significantly over the past century.
Life expectancy have risen significantly over the past century.
Life expectancy have rose significantly over the past century.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past century' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time help arrived, the patient's condition worsened.
By the time help had arrived, the patient's condition worsened.
By the time help arrived, the patient's condition have already worsened.
By the time help arrived, the patient's condition had already worsened.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'the patient's condition had already worsened.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Health officials are meeting next week to discuss the outbreak.
Health officials meet next week to discuss the outbreak.
Health officials will meeting next week to discuss the outbreak.
Health officials are meet next week to discuss the outbreak.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said she will schedule the surgery next month.
She said she would schedule the surgery next month.
She said she would scheduled the surgery next month.
She said she would have schedule the surgery next month.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'she said she would schedule the surgery.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish people take mental health more seriously.
I wish people have taken mental health more seriously.
I wish people took mental health more seriously.
I wish people would take mental health more seriously as a rule.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish people took mental health more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish doctors warned us earlier about the side effects.
I wish doctors have warned us earlier about the side effects.
I wish doctors would have warned us earlier about the side effects.
I wish doctors had warned us earlier about the side effects.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish doctors had warned us earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I had my blood pressure checked at the clinic yesterday.
I had checked my blood pressure at the clinic yesterday.
I had my blood pressure check at the clinic yesterday.
I have my blood pressure checked at the clinic yesterday.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had my blood pressure checked.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the hospital had treated so many patients in one day.
Never before had the hospital treated so many patients in one day.
Never before did the hospital treated so many patients in one day.
Never before has the hospital had treated so many patients in one day.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the hospital treated...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The health board is looking the cause of the outbreak into.
The health board is looking in to the cause of the outbreak.
The health board is looking into the cause of the outbreak.
The health board is looking into to the cause of the outbreak.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the cause of the outbreak.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What patients urgently need are a faster diagnosis system.
That patients urgently need is a faster diagnosis system.
What patients urgently need is faster diagnosis system it.
What patients urgently need is a faster diagnosis system.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What patients need is a faster diagnosis system.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some hospitals have modern equipment, whereas others still use outdated machines.
Some hospitals have modern equipment, whereas others still uses outdated machines.
Some hospitals have modern equipment whereas, others still use outdated machines.
Some hospitals have modern equipment despite others still use outdated machines.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others still use...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the new treatment, her symptoms persisted.
In spite of the new treatment, her symptoms persisted.
Despite of the new treatment, her symptoms persisted.
In spite of the new treatment, her symptoms persisted though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the new treatment, her symptoms persisted.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked poor sleep to weakened immunity.
The number of studies have linked poor sleep to weakened immunity.
A number of studies have linked poor sleep to weakened immunity.
A great number of studies has linked poor sleep to weakened immunity.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire nursing staff.
She spoke on behalf for the entire nursing staff.
She spoke behalf of the entire nursing staff.
She spoke on behalf of the entire nursing staff.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the staff.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The introduction of stricter hygiene protocols reduced infection rates significantly.
The introduce of stricter hygiene protocols reduced infection rates significantly.
The introducing of stricter hygiene protocols reduced infection rates significantly.
The introduction of stricter hygiene protocols reduce infection rates significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'introduce' becomes 'the introduction of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a hospital's visiting hours?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your visiting hours, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your visiting hours.
Just wanted to know about your visiting hours.
Hey, tell me about your visiting hours.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a delayed medical appointment?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about my delayed appointment.
I want to complain about my delayed appointment, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about the delay in my appointment.
I am writing to express my concern about the delay in my appointment, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results of the blood test were extreme alarming.
The results of the blood test were extremely alarm.
The results of the blood test were very much alarming.
The results of the blood test were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The new drug is more effective. Moreover, it has fewer side effects.
The new drug is more effective, moreover it has fewer side effects.
The new drug is more effective. Moreover it has fewer side effects.
The new drug is more effective moreover, it has fewer side effects.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The new drug is more effective. Moreover, it has fewer side effects.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd recommend regular checkups, didn't you?
You'd recommend regular checkups, wouldn't you?
You'd recommend regular checkups, would you?
You'd recommend regular checkups, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd recommend..., wouldn't you?'
